data.name: Atisha
data.long_meaning: Atisha (अतिशा) is a Sanskrit name meaning 'precious, invaluable, and serene'. It is derived from the Sanskrit words 'ati' (beyond) and 'isha' (lord). In Hindu mythology, Atisha is revered as a great master of Mahayana Buddhism. He is known for his profound wisdom and is considered an embodiment of compassion and enlightenment.

data.cultural_impact: Atisha is a significant name in the rich cultural tapestry of the Hindu tradition, particularly in the Mahayana Buddhist tradition. He was born in Bengal, India, in 982 AD, and his teachings have had a profound impact on various aspects of Hindu and Buddhist spirituality, philosophical thought, and cultural practices. He is often regarded as the founder of the Tibetan Mahayana Buddhist tradition, as he is credited with bringing Buddhist teachings from India to Tibet. In Hindu society, Atisha is remembered for his role in promoting peace, wisdom, and enlightenment, and his teachings have inspired generations of spiritual seekers.
data.spiritual_significance: Atisha is a name that represents spiritual excellence, wisdom, and compassion. In Hindu mythology, he is considered a great master who embodies these qualities. He is believed to have meritorious qualities beyond the ordinary, a precious being, and a source of enlightenment. His teachings emphasize the importance of loving-kindness, altruism, and the development of a compassionate heart. He is revered for his profound understanding of the nature of reality, the skillful means for attaining enlightenment, and the ability to convey these teachings to future generations. Through the grace of Atisha, one can tap into the boundless wisdom and compassion of the universe.

historical_references.reference: Atisha Dipamkara (980-1054 CE) was a famous Indian Buddhist scholar from Bengal. He is known for his role in the transmission of the Tibetan Buddhist tradition. Atisha brought the tantric teachings of the Sarvastivadin and Mahayana schools to Tibet, and also influenced the development of the Tibetan Mahayana school.

Atisha, or Atisa, was an influential Indian Buddhist master who is believed to have visited Tibet in the 11th century CE. He was a key figure in the dissemination of the Tibetan Mahayana tradition and was instrumental in the spread of certain esoteric Buddhist teachings. Atisha's teachings had a profound impact on the development of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism.
